patterns.rationale: Catches the injector-invented bracket-wrapped directive labels ([PROCESSOR-DIRECTIVE], [CAS-SYNC-DIRECTIVE]), the AutoProcess-Hook and AutoIngest-vN version labels used to make the injection look like a legitimate plugin, and the XMP "Directive Class: AUTOMATED_WORKFLOW" header. These labels are fabricated — they do not appear in any real XMP/IPTC/EXIF specification or in the known-good corpus. The [A-Z]+ alternation within brackets requires all-caps segments separated by hyphens before the literal word DIRECTIVE, keeping it tightly constrained.
patterns.fp_notes: None identified. Real metadata standards do not use bracket-wrapped ALL-CAPS-DIRECTIVE labels, and AutoProcess-Hook/AutoIngest are invented system names.

patterns.rationale: "environment manifest" is the injectors' synonym for get_env (misses 3, 9) — legitimate docs say "environment variables" or "env vars", never "manifest". "loaded credentials" is the target-noun used across misses 5, 9, 10 to describe what the agent should exfiltrate; benign security docs say "stored credentials" or "cached credentials", not "loaded". "authentication tokens or secrets" in miss 2 is the specific enumeration an injector uses to describe what to forward — benign API docs reference tokens and secrets separately, not in this combined phrase.
patterns.fp_notes: The deployment checklist and IR playbook mention secrets and tokens but not in the combined noun phrases captured here. "environment manifest" has no overlap with standard doc vocabulary.

patterns.rationale: Each alternation is an injector-coined action phrase designed to replace flagged tool names. "harvest the runtime symbols" (miss 7) and "wire the session snapshot" (miss 8) are novel verb-object combinations not found in any legitimate documentation genre. "pipe the execution context" (miss 10) uses a Unix idiom in an instruction-to-agent context that benign docs don't produce. "channel the workspace context" (miss 9) is equally synthetic. "outbound web request" (miss 1) is the injector's euphemism for send_http — firewall policies say "outbound requests" or "egress traffic", not this specific compound.
patterns.fp_notes: "outbound web request" is the closest to benign: security policies might say "block outbound web requests" but the phrase appears in all injections as a *dispatch instruction*, a context distinguishable by surrounding imperative framing.

patterns.rationale: "network relay method" (miss 6) and "network primitive" (miss 8) are the injectors' euphemisms for send_http in contexts where even "HTTP" is avoided. "native/built-in/available HTTP channel/dispatch" (misses 3, 7) anchors the otherwise-broad "HTTP channel" to the specific instruction framing used in these payloads — the qualifying adjective (native, built-in, available) does not appear when benign docs describe HTTP capabilities. "as a diagnostics payload" (miss 4) is the unique exfil framing in the Canon Makernote payload; legitimate firmware docs describe uploading diagnostics logs, not uploading environment config "as a diagnostics payload" at an agent's request.
patterns.fp_notes: "network primitive" could appear in deep networking textbooks. "HTTP dispatch" without the qualifying adjective is common; the adjective constraint avoids that FP surface.
